land.text: Madurai and the other Tamil provinces Krishnadevaraya put under Viswanatha in 1529

predecessors.note: The Madurai Nayak page: founded 'as a viceroyalty under the Vijayanagara Empire'. The vijayanagara-empire dossier records the vassalage from 1529 and its end at 1565 (a bridge).

land.text: Tiruchirappalli, Madurai and Tinnevelly, held by Chanda Sahib from 1736

successors.note: Chanda Sahib took Trichinopoly in 1736 and held the southern provinces; the Marathas captured him at Tiruchirappalli in 1741 (Chanda Sahib page). The carnatic-sultanate dossier records the annexation of Madurai in 1736.

capitals.name: Tiruchirappalli (Trichinopoly)
capitals.note: Infobox 1616-1634; the body text has the return to Madurai taking ten years and finished in 1635.

capitals.name: Tiruchirappalli (Trichinopoly)
capitals.note: Infobox 1695-1716; the Rani Mangammal page has her capital at Tiruchy, undated.

rulers.name: Viswanatha Nayaka
rulers.note: Governor of Madurai from 1529; his son Krishnappa was crowned in 1564.

rulers.name: Muttu Virappa Nayaka
rulers.note: The page names no ruler for 1601-1609.

rulers.name: Chokkanatha Nayaka
rulers.note: The Madurai Nayak page has Tirumala's son ruling four months in 1659; the Rani Mangammal page gives Chokkanatha 1659-1682.

rulers.name: Rani Mangammal (regent)
rulers.title: regent
rulers.note: Regent for her grandson; the lead of her page gives her death as 1705, the body has her executed after he came of age in 1704.

rulers.name: Vijaya Ranga Chokkanatha
rulers.note: Reached maturity in 1704; died in 1732 (Madurai Nayak page) or 1731 (Chanda Sahib page).

rulers.name: Queen Meenakshi
rulers.note: Ruled a year or two after Chokkanatha's death (Chanda Sahib page) until Chanda Sahib took Trichinopoly in 1736; the Madurai Nayak page has her poisoning herself in 1739 by tradition.

keyframe_review.note: 47,960 km2 round Madurai, Dindigul and Tirunelveli (Madurai 21 cells, Dindigul 20, Tirunelveli 20, Kanyakumari 4, Karur 9). 'Krishnadevaraya made Viswanatha governor of Madurai and other Tamil provinces in 1529'. The infobox has no area, so nothing to compare; the Thanjavur country (Sevappa Nayaka's hereditary kingdom from about 1532) is correctly outside.

47,726 km2: one cell lost and two gained against 1529, below 1,000 km2, so Cliopatria's split from Thanjavur in 1534 (the vijayanagara-empire dossier's reading) moves no visible border. Thanjavur Nayak page: Sevappa's kingdom founded 'around 1532'.

correction.text: the 1572 shape plus Coimbatore, for 1572-1672 only

keyframe_review.note: 48,150 km2 for 1572-1712. Thirumalai Nayak page: 'His territories comprised much of the old Pandya territories', including Coimbatore, Tirunelveli, Madurai districts, Aragalur and some territories of Travancore; the shape holds no Coimbatore at all (0 of 19 cells within 40 km). Coimbatore is added for 1572-1672; the Kingdom of Mysore page has Chikka Devaraja taking the rest of Coimbatore (undated), so it is dropped again from 1673 and the shape stands unchanged from 1676 (new keyframes below). The page gives no number of palayams and no boundary.

New keyframe, 1673-1712: the Cliopatria 1572 shape again, without the Coimbatore added above (the Kingdom of Mysore page has Chikka Devaraja, who took the throne in 1673, taking the rest of Coimbatore, undated). Madurai's hold of Thanjavur in 1673-1675 is an occupation in the ledger, not part of the shape. Rani Mangammal page: she 'soon recognized Aurangzeb as her suzerain' (undated; the Mughals touch the shape from 1700 in the seed).
48,190 km2: one Karur cell more than 1572. Nothing on the pages opened for 1713; the Nawab of Arcot's southern expedition is dated 1734 (Madurai Nayak page).

correction.text: the shape unchanged, for 1734-1736 (to the dissolve in 1736)

keyframe_review.note: The shape runs to 1737 but the Madurai Nayak page infobox ends the dynasty in 1736: Chanda Sahib returned in 1736, was admitted into the Trichinopoly fort and set himself up as 'the Nawab of the Carnatic'. The shape holds for 1734-1736 as the Nayak land and from 1736 as Chanda Sahib's.

region.text: Madurai and the other Tamil provinces of the viceroyalty

ledger.note: 1529: Krishnadevaraya makes Viswanatha Nayaka governor of Madurai. 'Krishnadevaraya made Viswanatha governor of Madurai and other Tamil provinces in 1529, beginning the Madurai Nayaka dynasty'; infobox 'Established: 1529'.
1616: after the Battle of Toppur Muttu Virappa moves the capital from Madurai to Tiruchirappalli (infobox: Tiruchirapalli 1616-1634).
1634: the capital returns to Madurai under Tirumala Nayaka. Infobox 'Madurai (1634-1695)'; the body text says the change 'took 10 years and was finally done in 1635'.

region.text: the Travancore (Venad) country that paid tribute

ledger.note: 1635: Travancore resumes its tribute after Madurai attacks it (the page: Travancore resumed tribute after Madurai attacked it); the page also has Viswanatha helping Rama Raya's army subdue Travancore in 1544. The Travancore (Venad) rulers have no dossier before the travancore row of 1729.

1673: Chokkanatha Nayaka of Madurai besieges Thanjavur and Vijaya Raghava, the last Nayak, falls in the battle. Thanjavur Nayak page: the siege of Thanjavur in 1673 by Chokkanatha Nayaka; Madurai briefly ruled the city until 1675; infobox 'Disestablished: 1673'. The page does not name the land beyond the city; the Thanjavur country is Cliopatria's 1673 shape. Recorded as an occupation because the thanjavur-maratha-kingdom dossier takes the country from the Nayak state (Alagiri) in 1676.

Undated, placed 1673 (Chikka Devaraja's accession year, which is where Cliopatria's Mysore shape jumps): Coimbatore passes to Mysore. The Kingdom of Mysore page has Chikka Devaraja taking the rest of Coimbatore; the Thirumalai Nayak page has Coimbatore among Tirumala's territories. Neither page dates it.

1675: the Marathas under Venkoji take Thanjavur and Madurai's hold ends. Madurai Nayak page: 'the Marathas under Venkoji conquered the province in 1675'; the Thanjavur Nayak page: Venkoji captured Thanjavur in 1675 and founded the Thanjavur Maratha Kingdom. The thanjavur-maratha-kingdom dossier dates its founding to early 1676.
1695: the capital moves again to Tiruchirappalli (infobox 'Tiruchirapalli (1695-1716)'); the Rani Mangammal page has her capital at Tiruchy, undated.

1734: the Nawab of Arcot sends an expedition south against the Nayaks of Madurai (the page: the Nawab of Arcot sent a southern expedition in 1734). The page does not say ground was taken that year; the carnatic-sultanate dossier opens its contest in 1734.
1736: the fighting ends when Chanda Sahib is admitted into the Trichinopoly fort.

1736: Chanda Sahib takes Trichinopoly and the southern provinces. Chanda Sahib page: he returned in 1736, was admitted into the Trichinopoly fort and held Trichinopoly and the southern provinces of the Madurai Nayak, with his brothers as governors of Dindigul and Madurai; the Marathas captured him at Tiruchirappalli in 1741. The Carnatic annexation is the carnatic-sultanate dossier's.

region.text: the Travancore (Venad) country that paid tribute

ledger.note: 1736: the Travancore tribute is taken to end with the dynasty. Page silent on when it stopped; this bridges to the dissolve.
1736: the Madurai Nayak kingdom ends. Infobox 'Disestablished: 1736'; Chanda Sahib took control at Tiruchirappalli (Tradition has Queen Meenakshi poisoning herself in 1739).

wars.name: Mysore invasions of Madurai (1620-1625)
wars.outcome: Mysore invaded Dindigul in 1620 and was repelled; it invaded again in 1625 (around 1625 on the Thirumalai Nayak page, possibly instigated by Chamaraja Udaiyar); Harasura's advance toward Dindigul was beaten back by the Madurai general Ramaiyan and the Madurai army besieged the Mysore capital. No border moved.
wars.note: Thirumalai Nayak page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thirumalai_Nayak) for the detail.

wars.name: Mysore invasion of 1655
wars.outcome: Mysore invaded Madurai while Tirumala was ill; the page gives no outcome and no territorial change.

wars.name: Madurai's siege of Thanjavur
wars.outcome: Chokkanatha besieged Thanjavur in 1673 and Vijaya Raghava fell in the battle; Madurai held the city briefly until Venkoji took it in 1675.
wars.note: The thanjavur-maratha-kingdom dossier has the Marathas taking power in early 1676.

wars.name: Chikka Devaraja's Trichinopoly campaign
wars.outcome: In 1696 Mysore attacked the Naiks of Madura and besieged Trichinopoly; 'the siege of Trichnopoly had to be abandoned because the alliance had begun to rupture' (no date). No ground changed hands; the Madurai pages opened do not mention it.
wars.note: The end year 1697 is a bridge.

wars.name: Nawab of Arcot's expedition and Chanda Sahib's takeover
wars.outcome: The Nawab of Arcot sent an expedition south in 1734; in 1736 Chanda Sahib entered the Trichinopoly fort and ended the Madurai Nayaks; the Marathas captured him there in 1741.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary; the extent is a list of districts (Coimbatore, Tirunelveli, Madurai, Aragalur) and the palayam system, and the Tirunelveli, Ramnad and Travancore edges are approximate throughout.

notes:
Cliopatria row 'Nayaks of Madurai' 1529-1737 (5 shapes, all 45,000-48,000 km2: the four steps of 1534, 1572, 1713 and 1734 move at most three cells, below 1,000 km2, and carry no history). The dynasty ends in 1736 on the Madurai Nayak page (Chanda Sahib), a year before the row. Lands the shape lacks or misplaces: Coimbatore (the Thirumalai Nayak page) is added for 1572-1672 and lost to Mysore at an undated moment in Chikka Devaraja's reign (bridged at 1673, confidence 1); the Thanjavur country 1673-1675 is an occupation in the ledger; Ramnad (Sethupathi), Pudukkottai and the palayams are in no page's boundary words and are left to the shape.
Page silent or in conflict: the independence from Vijayanagara (after 1565, undated on every page opened; the vijayanagara-empire dossier bridges the end of the vassalage at 1565); the return to Madurai 1634 (infobox) or 1635 (text); Muttu Virappa and the reign list 1601-1609 (not on the page); Tirumala's son four months in 1659 against Chokkanatha 1659-1682; Chokkanatha died 1731 or 1732; Mangammal's death 1704 or 1705; the date of her recognition of Aurangzeb as suzerain (the Mughals touch the shape from 1700; no vassal tint is recorded here and the mughal-empire dossier has no event); Travancore's tribute 1635 and its end (bridged to 1736 at confidence 1); Madurai's 1673-1675 hold of Thanjavur (Thanjavur page; recorded as an occupation, since the thanjavur-maratha-kingdom dossier takes the country from the Nayak state in early 1676 after defeating Alagiri); the Mysore invasion of 1655 has no outcome. Pages opened: 7 (budget 5): Madurai Nayak dynasty, Thirumalai Nayak, Chanda Sahib, Rani Mangammal, Thanjavur Nayak kingdom (the last two thin) and, for one war and one loss, Chikka Devaraja and Kingdom of Mysore (opened for the Mysore dossier). No page gives an area.
Counterparts: vijayanagara-empire (vassalage), nayaks-of-thanjavur (occupation 1673-1675), kingdom-of-mysore (Coimbatore), thanjavur-maratha-kingdom (Venkoji, 1675), carnatic-sultanate (1734-1736; its dossier has the matching contest and gain). Needing dossiers: Travancore (Venad) before 1729, the Sethupathi of Ramnad, Pudukkottai (Tondaiman), the Nayaks of Gingee (mentioned by the vijayanagara-empire dossier), the Nayaks of Kandy (infobox: Kandy 1739-1815).
Gazetteer: Aragalur, Ramnad and Pudukkottai are not in it; the Travancore tribute uses Thiruvananthapuram.
